get.description:
Returns the products in your account that match your filters, one page at a time. With no filters, it returns every product, including archived ones.

Use it to look up products by SKU or any other field, to export your catalog page by page, or to find products that changed after a given date.

Filters are query parameters written as `field=value` or `field[operator]=value`. A product must match all of them, unless you group filters with `_or`. Besides the top-level fields, you can filter on:

- Custom attributes, through `attributes.<label>`, for example `attributes.material=Canvas`
- Related records, through dot paths such as `categories.name`
- A parent's direct variants, through `parent_id=<id>` or `parent.sku=<sku>`

A few filter details to plan for:

- For a case-insensitive match, use `contains:ignorecase`. `icontains` isn't an operator and returns `400`.
- A date filter with an invalid date, such as `modified[gte]=not-a-date`, returns an empty list instead of an error.

Results come back 25 per page by default, up to 1000 with `_page_size`. To get the next page, follow `pagination.next_page`. On the last page that key is left out, not set to `null`. The link starts with `http://`, so change it to `https://` before you follow it. Otherwise the redirect can drop your `Authorization` header. The response doesn't include a total count.

For a stable order while you page through a large result set, sort by `id`, which follows creation order. Each page is a separate request. See [Rate limits](/docs/reference/v3/rate-limits).

Related pages:

- [Filtering and query syntax](/docs/reference/v3/filtering-query-syntax)
- [Pagination](/docs/reference/v3/pagination)
- [Export your full catalog](/docs/guides/exporting-your-full-catalog)
- [Audit product data quality with filters](/docs/guides/auditing-product-data-quality-with-filters)

- Comparison: `eq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`
- Presence: `exists`, `null`

patch.description:

- `label` can't be changed. Sending it returns `422`. Products keep their values under the same `attributes.<label>` key.
- `type` can't be changed.
- `name` can be changed. Renaming doesn't change `label`.

Group membership and product family membership aren't changed here. To link the attribute to a product family, use [Link an attribute to a product family](/docs/reference/v3/familyattributes/create-family-attribute).

OperationResponse.title: OperationResponse
OperationResponse.description:
Standard response envelope for every non-DELETE operation.

Exactly one of ``data`` / ``errors`` is populated:

* GET / CREATE / BULK_CREATE / BULK_DELETE / BULK_PATCH / UPDATE success → ``data`` is the returned object/value.
* SEARCH success → ``data`` is a list of results.
* Failure → ``errors`` is set, ``data`` is an empty list.

Example::

    # GET / CREATE / BULK_CREATE / BULK_DELETE / BULK_PATCH / UPDATE success
    OperationResponse(data={"id": 1, "name": "Widget"})

    # SEARCH success
    OperationResponse(data=[{"id": 1, "name": "Widget"}])

An error-shaped instance (``errors`` set) is what a registered exception
handler returns — see :mod:`plytix_api_tools.core.exception_registry`.
Application code signals failure by raising, not by constructing one of
these directly.
